key_insight: Cross-task parameter sharing can turn self-reinforcement into a collective instability: with enough uncertain training problems, label-free RLVR may maximize self-agreement while accuracy collapses.
engineering_relevance: Scaling label-free RLVR to more problems can increase collapse risk, making shared-update structure and initial model confidence important design considerations.
method: Derive a solvable coupled-task model comparing per-problem sharpening with shared-mode amplification.
Predict a critical dataset size controlled by coupling strength, initial confidence, and perturbation size.
Test predictions in simulations and a small Transformer; analyze protective coupling and marginal-entropy regularization.
evidence_signal: Simulations reproduce the predicted transition and approximate inverse-square coupling dependence, while small-Transformer experiments show that removing the shared direction prevents collapse and restoring it causes collapse.
watch_item: The abstract reports model simulations and small-Transformer experiments, so effectiveness of the proposed stabilizers at larger scales remains unestablished.
paper_title: Collective Dynamics of Self-Reinforcement: How Cross-Task Coupling Drives Policy Collapse in Unsupervised RLVR
